tasks.title: Connect two computers
tasks.statement: Two computers are already configured: addresses 192.168.0.1 and 192.168.0.2 on the same subnet. But there is no link between them. Click “Cable”, pick the first node, then the second, and test the connection with ping.
tasks.hint: A link is an edge of the graph. Without a cable the nodes cannot exchange even a single packet.

tasks.title: A switch in the middle
tasks.statement: Four computers, all on the same subnet 192.168.0.0/24, and one switch. Run a cable from each computer to the switch. A computer has just one port, while a switch connects many at once. Check that every computer can reach every other.
tasks.hint: The switch has eight ports. Each computer plugs into its own port with its own cable.

tasks.title: Short path versus long path
tasks.statement: There are two paths to the server: through the “Fast” router (20 km cables) and through the “Slow” one (1500 km each). The PC currently uses the long path, hence the high propagation delay (about 5 µs per kilometer). Open the PC terminal, look at ping and traceroute, then switch the default gateway to the fast router.
tasks.hint: Start with `ip route`: it has a default line. Delete it with `ip route del default`, then run `ip route add default via 10.0.1.1`. The address 10.0.1.1 is “Fast” on the PC side.

spec_text./goals/0/text: The server responds in under 5 ms

tasks.title: Why doesn't it ping?
tasks.statement: PC 1 can reach neither PC 2 nor the server. The addresses are configured correctly, there are no address errors. Find and fix two faults at the lower layers, physical and data link. Hint: look at what `ip link` shows in the terminal and check that all cables are in place.
tasks.hint: One port is disabled in software (`ip link set eth0 up` on the right computer), and the server has no cable: add one with “Cable”.

spec_text./goals/2/text: PC 2 opens port 80 on the server

tasks.title: Two networks and a router
tasks.statement: PC A lives in the network 192.168.1.0/24, PC B in 192.168.2.0/24. A router connects them, and it is already configured. But the computers do not know where to send packets for the other network. This is how the internet works: a network of networks. Give each computer a default gateway: the router's address in its own network.
tasks.hint: The command is `ip route add default via <router address>`. The gateway for PC A is 192.168.1.1, for PC B 192.168.2.1.
